The '''2025–26 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Iowa]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Hawkeyes, led by first-year head coach [[Ben McCollum]], played their home games at [[Carver–Hawkeye Arena]] in [[Iowa City, Iowa]] as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]].

Iowa opened the season with seven straight wins, including winning the [[Acrisure Classic]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Iowa secures Acrisure Classic crown over Grand Canyon |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/iowa-secures-ariscure-classic-crown-over-grand-canyon--flm-2025-11-27/ |newspaper=[[Reuters]] |date=November 27, 2025 |access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> The team was ranked in the AP poll for three weeks before finishing the regular season with a 10–10 record in [[2025–26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]]. The Hawkeyes played as the No. 9 seed in the [[2026 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]]. They defeated No. 17 seed [[2025–26 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]] in the second round before falling to No. 8 seed [[2025–26 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]], 72–69,<ref>{{cite web |title=Buckeyes Survive Nail-biter to Advance in Big Ten Tournament |url=https://bigten.org/blog/59609/ |publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 12, 2026 |access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> in the third round.

The Hawkeyes received an at-large bid to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 9 seed in the South region.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ben McCollum sparks another turnaround as Iowa returns to the NCAA Tournament, Clemson on deck |url=https://apnews.com/article/march-madness-iowa-8c7fd7d64ce6138102737be7d6c83704 |newspaper=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 16, 2026 |access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> Iowa defeated No. 8 seed [[2025–26 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]] 67–61 in the first round.<ref>{{cite news |title=Stirtz weathers cold shooting to score 16 and help Iowa beat Clemson 67-61 in March Madness |url=https://apnews.com/article/iowa-clemson-march-madness-score-c164f86796211c540fefa45ac500e08f |newspaper=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 20, 2026 |access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> In the second round, Iowa faced No. 1 seed and defending National champion [[2025–26 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Florida Gators and Iowa Hawkeyes meet in NCAA Tournament second round |url=https://apnews.com/article/florida-gators-college-sports-florida-iowa-iowa-hawkeyes-825103e412784266b6dc077fe4e1629f |newspaper=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 22, 2026 |access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> With 4.5 seconds left, junior [[Alvaro Folgueiras]] made a game-winning 3-pointer to give the Hawkeyes the win, 73–72. The win sent Iowa to the Sweet Sixteen for the first time since 1999. It was also Iowa's first victory over a No. 1 seed in the NCAA Tournament since 1980.<ref>{{cite news |title=Iowa beats No. 1 seed and defending champ Florida in March Madness on Folgueiras’ 3 in final seconds |url=https://apnews.com/article/iowa-florida-score-march-madness-aa80c53cb290b3bd6b6d69aa387c44e2 |newspaper=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 22, 2026 |access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> In the regional semifinal, the Hawkeyes faced a familiar opponent in No. 4 seed [[2025–26 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]]. Despite trailing for nearly the first 38 minutes of the game, Iowa took the lead with 2:11 remaining on a 3-pointer from [[Bennett Stirtz]] and never trailed again, en route to a 77–71 victory. The win moved the Hawkeyes into the Elite Eight for the first time since 1987.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ninth-seeded Iowa continues improbable March run, beating Nebraska 77-71 to reach Elite Eight |url=https://apnews.com/article/iowa-nebraska-score-march-madness-94c5c63fec9c3078e9efde7e1d539f29 |newspaper=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 26, 2026 |access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> In the South region final, Iowa faced another Big Ten opponent in No. 3 seed [[2025–26 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]]. The Hawkeyes jumped to an early double-digit lead and led by four at halftime. After numerous second-half lead changes, the Illini pulled away late and prevailed 71–59, ending Iowa's season with a 24–13 record.<ref>{{cite news |title=Illinois powers its way to its first Final Four in 21 years, beating Iowa 71-59 |url=https://apnews.com/article/iowa-illinois-march-madness-score-4f4ce827f43e80e2967a02518f5e1dd7 |newspaper=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 28, 2026 |access-date=March 29, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Ben McCollum’s winning legacy continues with Iowa’s March Madness run |url=https://apnews.com/article/iowa-ben-mccollum-march-madness-fc5bc390c253b2e503d13075b07d8555 |newspaper=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 28, 2026 |access-date=March 29, 2026}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2024–25 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Hawkeyes]] finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] 17–16, 7–13 in [[2023–24 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a five-way tie for twelfth place. As the No. 15 seed in the [[2025 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they beat [[2024–25 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] in the first round,<ref>{{cite web |title=Harding hits late 3 to help Iowa pull away and beat Ohio State 77-70 in a Big Ten Tournament opener |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401743894 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 26, 2025 |date=March 12, 2025}}</ref> before losing to [[2024–25 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] in the quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kylan Boswell scores 24 points to help No. 24 Illinois beat Iowa 106-94 in Big Ten tourney |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401743918 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=June 27, 2025 |date=March 13, 2025}}</ref> The loss would be the final game of the season and the final game for [[Fran McCaffery]] as head coach at Iowa, as the Hawkeyes opted out of postseason play following the firing of McCaffery.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tachman |first1=Tyler |title=Iowa basketball won't participate in postseason tournament following Fran McCaffery departure |url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2025/03/15/iowa-basketball-fran-mccaffery-postseason-tournament-nit-crown-hawkeyes-big-ten/82442869007/ |website=Hawk Central |access-date=June 27, 2025 |date=March 15, 2025}}</ref>

On March 14, 2025, the school fired head coach Fran McCaffery.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Thamel |first1=Pete |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |title=Iowa dismisses head coach Fran McCaffery after 15 seasons |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44251986/sources-iowa-set-dismiss-head-coach-fran-mccaffery |website=ESPN.com |access-date=June 27, 2025 |date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> On March 24, the school hired [[Drake Bulldogs men's basketball|Drake]] head coach [[Ben McCollum]] to be their next head coach.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Thamel |first1=Pete |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |title=Iowa hires Drake's Ben McCollum as men's basketball coach |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44384134/sources-iowa-hire-drake-ben-mccollum-head-coach |website=ESPN.com |access-date=June 27, 2025 |date=March 24, 2025}}</ref>
